q0848: Deliberately exposing risky services (SMB, RDP) to the internet in an isolated segment = honeynet bait.
q0849: Guest account ends up in the admin group = privilege escalation.
q0850: Immediate restoration = hot site. Warm = hours to days. Cold = days to weeks.
q0851: Certificate created and signed internally, not by a public CA = self-signed.
q0852: RTO = how long you can be down. RPO = how much data you can lose.
q0853: Wi-Fi reaching neighboring buildings → heat map to see where the signal leaks, then reduce power or move APs.
q0854: Confirm a file hasn't changed = hashing (integrity).
q0855: Recovery site lacks enough hardware or storage = a capacity planning failure.
q0856: Protection that disappears when the VPN drops → put it on the host (host-based content filter).
q0858: Admin passwords stored in a shared document → password manager/vault.
q0859: Compromise a site a specific group visits (developers, one industry) = watering hole.
q0860: Internal audit's main benefit: finding control gaps to fix before external auditors or attackers do.
q0861: Employee installs unapproved tech (rogue router, personal cloud) with no malicious intent = shadow IT.
q0862: Extended power outage = generator. UPS/batteries only bridge minutes.
q0863: Browser certificate warning on an internal HTTPS site = self-signed certificate (not trusted by the browser).
q0864: Before a change is implemented it needs approval → management review (a CAB). Load testing and notices aren't approval steps.
q0865: Bug bounty benefits: vulnerabilities found faster and a better security reputation. It doesn't cut costs.
q0866: Breaking out of a guest VM to reach the host = VM escape.
q0868: Find out WHICH users fall for phishing → phishing simulation campaign that tracks clicks.
q0869: Stop bloatware or unwanted apps from running → application allow list.
q0871: Keep records for a required period before disposal = data retention.
q0872: Logins from far-apart locations minutes apart = impossible travel.
q0873: DRP needs a site for immediate continued operations = hot site.
q0874: MDM blocks jailbreaking so users can't modify the mobile OS or bypass its controls.
q0875: Zero-day on systems that can't go down → compensating controls + monitoring until a patch exists.
q0876: MDM checks that a device meets policy before it gets corporate access = compliance attestation.
q0877: Heavy SMB (TCP 445) traffic across the whole network with outages = worm spreading.
